 Domantas Sabonis produced 11 points (3-of-6 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and three assists in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 Sabonis’ season-long fantasy value has been solid, with the Kings’ center providing top-50 per-game value. However, he has had a few rough performances. Sabonis recorded a double-double against the Thunder, but the shot attempts were surprisingly low on a night when the Kings were down Zach LaVine and De’Andre Hunter. Sabonis’ average of 8.8 field-goal attempts per game is his lowest since his rookie season (5.9 in 2016-17). 
 Domantas Sabonis 
 SAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #11 
 Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers. 
 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far. 
 Domantas Sabonis 
 SAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #11 
 Domantas Sabonis shot 0-of-2 from the field and 0-of-2 from the foul line in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic, going scoreless with two rebounds and five assists. 
 To say that Sabonis had a Tuesday night to forget would be an understatement. For the first time in his career, he failed to score a point in a game in which he played at least 20 minutes. Interestingly, Sabonis didn’t take his first shot until about two minutes into the fourth quarter. Given his production so far this season, fantasy managers shouldn’t overreact to Sabonis’ showing against the Magic. That said, it will raise some eyebrows.

 Domantas Sabonis had 17 points (8-of-12 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer on Friday against the Spurs. 
 Sabonis had another efficient night, getting his way with another double-double. The two-man game with Darius Acuff has helped his efficiency, even though he isn’t getting the ball much. His efficiency could drop to 56 percent over his career instead of 68.8 percent now, but his value feels relatively stable since his role on this team isn’t going to change. 
 Domantas Sabonis 
 SAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #11 
 Domantas Sabonis had 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), 17 rebounds, an assist, and a steal in the 116-103 loss to the Lakers. 
 At the end of the game, he was holding his ribs and grimacing in pain as he went to the locker room, so it’s something to keep an eye on. The two-man game with Acuff has been effective on the offensive end. The usage of Sabonis has gone done dramatically and he’s shooting very efficiently from the field this year at 69.1% when the best season he had apart from this year was 61.5% in the 22-23 season. If the efficiency drops, then Sabonis will likely have more of a drop off in the points category with how much Acuff has had the ball. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (elbow) recorded 23 points (8-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 After attempting nine shots in Saturday’s blowout loss to the Grizzlies, LaVine got up 14 on Monday. Fantasy managers will be pleased with his efficiency: LaVine shot over 50 percent from the field and made five of nine three-point attempts. With the Kings handing the keys to Darius Acuff Jr., there have been nights when LaVine and Domantas Sabonis (9/7/4/1) don’t get the touches they want. That can be a challenge for fantasy managers, especially if neither LaVine nor Sabonis gets moved before the February trade deadline.

 Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday. 
 Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points Wednesday, but a late technical foul proved costly in the loss to the Nuggets. The 28-year-old forward was assessed a technical foul in the final seconds of the game for throwing the ball in the direction of an official. This allowed Jamal Murray to make the technical free throw and ice the game for the Nuggets by extending the Denver lead to four. The Celtics begin a back-to-back against the Kings and Warriors on the road Saturday.

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Wednesday’s loss to the Suns with 36 points (11-of-22 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two blocks and six three-pointers.
 Since the 1976-77 season, only one player has scored more points in his first 13 NBA games than Acuff: Michael Jordan. The Kings rookie is in rarefied air, which makes his languishing on a team of this caliber so disappointing. Acuff was efficient as a scorer and playmaker on Wednesday, shooting 50 percent from the field and committing two turnovers. He’s definitely going to get his numbers, but he won’t win many games this season. It’s fair to wonder if there will come a point soon when the front office decides to move on from head coach Doug Christie.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Green accounted for 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
 After a slow start to the season, Green may be turning things around. He scored an efficient 16 points in Monday’s win over the Nuggets and had another productive outing against the Kings. His value, especially in category leagues, has been poor, but Green’s status as a starter is why he remains rostered in 66 percent of Yahoo leagues. The Suns visit the Jazz on Friday in their final game of the week.

 Devin Booker amassed 29 points (10-of-18 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Kings.
 After scoring 30 points in a November 12 win over the Hornets, Booker shot 9-of-28 from the field in games against the Lakers and Nuggets. He had a much better night against the Kings, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line while also dishing out six assists. Phoenix, which started 1-5, is now 6-2 over its last eight games, and Booker has provided top-25 fantasy value, as expected.

 Dillon Brooks finished Wednesday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (12-of-18 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and five three-pointers.
 In the six games he played before Wednesday, Brooks averaged 9.5 points per game while shooting 33.8 percent from the field. He and his teammates had the good fortune of playing against the Kings, and “The Villain” had his most productive game of the season. While Brooks didn’t record any defensive stats, he finished with a season-high point total and shot 66.7 percent from the field. The Suns play one more game this week, as they’ll visit the Jazz on Friday.

 Jokić had a great game Wednesday in the win over the Celtics. The 31-year-old center finished with 24 points, made three three-pointers and was just two rebounds and one assist away from another triple-double. Jokić is still a top-three player in fantasy basketball. The Nuggets have two games remaining this week, starting with a home matchup against the Rockets on Friday.
